qs.q: Which plasma protein is primarily responsible for generating the colloid osmotic pressure that prevents tissue edema?
qs.e: Albumin is the major plasma protein maintaining intravascular oncotic pressure and fluid balance.

qs.q: Which plasma protein commonly decreases during intravascular hemolysis because it binds free hemoglobin?
qs.e: Free plasma hemoglobin binds haptoglobin, lowering measurable haptoglobin during intravascular hemolysis.

qs.q: Which of the following plasma proteins has the highest affinity but lowest capacity for binding thyroxine (T4)? ---
qs.e: Transthyretin binds T4 with higher affinity than albumin but has a lower binding capacity. Thyroxine-binding globulin has high affinity and greater capacity than transthyretin.

ai.subject: Pathology
ai.summary: Plasma proteins maintain oncotic pressure, transport substances, and mediate immune responses. Their loss or dysfunction leads to edema, hypoalbuminaemia, and impaired immunity, especially in infections common in low‑resource settings.

sections.p: Plasma proteins are soluble proteins in blood plasma, mainly albumin, globulins, and fibrinogen. Diagnosis focuses on serum protein electrophoresis and albumin concentration.

t.b: Low albumin suggests loss (renal, hepatic, GI) or decreased synthesis.
A spike indicates plasma cell dyscrasia or lymphoma.
High ratio points to nephrotic syndrome or glomerulonephritis.

sections.p: Severity is graded by albumin level and clinical edema. Staging of nephrotic syndrome follows proteinuria and hypoalbuminaemia thresholds.
Loss of plasma proteins occurs via kidneys, liver, gut, or skin. Infections and inflammatory states increase capillary permeability.
Patients develop generalized edema, ascites, pleural effusion, and fatigue. Infections may worsen due to impaired transport of antibodies.
Key tests assess protein loss, synthesis, and immune status.

sections.p: Rapid weight gain, respiratory distress, or altered mental status suggest fluid overload or severe hypoalbuminaemia.

sections.p: Monitor albumin, edema, and renal function. Prevent infections and malnutrition.
